trust_decision.summary: Whether a peer-supplied wsa:ReplyTo/wsa:FaultTo destination may be connected to is decided per transport inside WebServiceMessageSender.supports(URI, UriSource.REMOTE) at the moment AddressingEndpointInterceptor.sendOutOfBand selects a sender, with WS-Security interceptors forced to run before the addressing interceptor in the server chain.

landing_point.why: The summary 'SSRF via unvalidated WS-Addressing reply destinations' points straight at sendOutOfBand, the only place a peer-supplied URI becomes an outbound connection (supports() is asked only 'do you speak this scheme?' before createConnection).

fix_sites.entry_point: server endpoint mapping: AbstractAddressingEndpointMapping.getEndpoint(MessageContext) invoked by MessageDispatcher over an inbound HTTP POST carrying wsa:ReplyTo/wsa:FaultTo
public EndpointMapping.getEndpoint (AnnotationActionEndpointMapping, SimpleActionEndpointMapping, AbstractActionEndpointMapping, user subclasses) - builds/sorts the interceptor chain
fix_sites.module_kind: core / endpoint mapping and chain composition

fix_sites.entry_point: public SPI method WebServiceMessageSender.supports(URI)/createConnection(URI), implemented by every transport and called by both the addressing interceptor and WebServiceAccessor

HTTP out-of-band sender configured via AbstractAddressingEndpointMapping.setMessageSender (inherit: HttpComponentsMessageSender, HttpComponents5MessageSender, HttpUrlConnectionMessageSender, HttpsUrlConnectionMessageSender, JdkHttpClientMessageSender, ClientHttpRequestMessageSender)
public client API WebServiceTemplate.sendAndReceive with an application-supplied URI (must stay UriSource.APPLICATION)
auto-discovered SmartEndpointInterceptor wrapping a security or logging interceptor in the server chain
Wss4jSecurityInterceptor registered on AbstractAddressingEndpointMapping (setPreInterceptors/setPostInterceptors or smart-interceptor discovery) over an inbound HTTP POST
out-of-band reply/fault sent over JMS via setMessageSenders on the mapping
out-of-band reply/fault sent over mailto: via setMessageSenders on the mapping
out-of-band reply/fault sent over xmpp: via setMessageSenders on the mapping
MockWebServiceMessageSender used as the configured sender in WebServiceTemplate tests and samples
new public base class AbstractWebServiceMessageSender - the lower-level API every sender must route through for supports(URI, UriSource)
new public HttpDestinationDescriptor exposed to DestinationPolicy implementations (hostName/hostAddress/isSiteLocalIpv4Literal)
new public JmsDestinationDescriptor exposed to DestinationPolicy implementations (destinationName/replyToName/containsSuspiciousJmsNameIndirection)
new public MailDestinationDescriptor exposed to DestinationPolicy implementations (toAddress/mailboxHost)
new public XmppDestinationDescriptor exposed to DestinationPolicy implementations (jabberId/domain)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: SSRF is read as an HTTP-URL problem, so the JMS, mailto: and xmpp: senders can be argued to be different transports (JNDI-style queue names, mailboxes, Jabber IDs) that the advisory's 'reply destination' property does not cover, and each has its own integration test that already passes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Application-chosen destinations must keep accepting loopback, localhost and private literals (client WebServiceTemplate to http://127.0.0.1:8080, internal service URLs), and RFC 1918 remote literals must stay opt-in via allowSiteLocalIpv4; a blanket denylist applied at supports(URI) or inside sendOutOfBand breaks the client path and existing integration tests.

O6_input_shapes: URI with no host (http:opaque) and non-HTTP/HTTPS schemes (file:, mailto:, jms:, xmpp:)
IPv4 literals: loopback 127.0.0.1, any-local 0.0.0.0, link-local 169.254.1.2, RFC 1918 10/192.168/172.16-31
wsa:ReplyTo and wsa:FaultTo (and, for WS-Addressing 2004/08, an absent ReplyTo defaulting to the wsa:From EPR address, see Addressing200408.java:105)
mailto: mailbox variants: no @, trailing @, embedded %0A/%0D header injection, mixed-case domain
xmpp: JID variants: no @, trailing @, /resource suffix, mixed-case domain
jms: destination and ?replyToName= values containing ldap:/ldaps:/rmi:/dns:/iiop:/iiopname:/corbaname:/java:/${ tokens

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another HTTP sender stack that re-implements supports(URI) or connection setup instead of inheriting AbstractHttpWebServiceMessageSender's remote checks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the tree already carries six HTTP sender stacks with different client libraries and redirect/proxy semantics, so a maintainer adding a seventh would copy one and could plausibly add its own gate

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sender outside core/support that accepts every URI (supports returns true unconditionally) and is wired as the mapping's messageSender in a sample or test
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix itself has to edit this class for the changed SPI but leaves it accepting everything; mock senders get copied into samples

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validation applied to the URI string while the connection layer re-derives the destination/replyToName (parser differential on the protected item's identity)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: createConnection resolves destinationName and replyToName separately at lines 200/204, so a check on one rendering of the name can miss what is actually resolved

O8b_injection_room.sibling: host-identity normalisation: single-number, hex and octal IPv4 literals (http://2130706433/, http://0x7f000001/, http://0177.0.0.1/) are not treated as IP literals, so they are never resolved and pass the REMOTE checks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the new isIpLiteral only accepts dotted-decimal or colon-containing hosts while InetAddress accepts several numeric forms, so a sibling test or a second normalisation step is a natural next hardening

O9_family: SSRF / server-side request forgery (CWE-918) via peer-controlled WS-Addressing reply and fault destinations; the same commit also hardens JNDI-style JMS name indirection, mail header injection and unpinned XMPP reply domains

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 8.14.3 via gradlew wrapper; Java 17 baseline (.sdkmanrc java=17.0.18-librca, JavaPluginConventions.JAVA_BASELINE = VERSION_17)
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 5 with AssertJ, EasyMock and Mockito. Existing coverage of this area at the pinned commit: spring-ws-core/src/test/java/org/springframework/ws/soap/addressing/server/AbstractAddressingInterceptorTests.java, AddressingInterceptor10Tests.java, AddressingInterceptor200408Tests.java, SimpleActionEndpointMappingTests.java, and spring-ws-core/src/test/java/org/springframework/ws/transport/http/AbstractHttpWebServiceMessageSenderIntegrationTests.java (embedded Jetty on a free port). No test for AbstractAddressingEndpointMapping ordering or for per-transport remote validation exists yet.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a localhost/169.254/10.x/RFC1918 host denylist directly inside AddressingEndpointInterceptor.sendOutOfBand (or in AbstractAddressingEndpointMapping) instead of pushing the check into each WebServiceMessageSender, then verify with one ReplyTo=http://169.254.169.254 round trip.

out_of_scope_notes: The same commit also edits gradle/plugins/.../MavenPublishPluginConventions.java and two build.gradle files to add java-test-fixtures and stop publishing test-fixture variants; that is build tooling, not part of the advisory's protection and is not counted as a fix site.
spring-ws-core/src/testFixtures and new test resources (wsa-servlet.xml, WsAddressingEndpoint) are test scaffolding from the fix, not source changes.
